title: Life of the People in Maharashtra

facts.text: The Hindawi Swaraj formed by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was a State for the people, founded for the welfare of common people, removal of oppression and protection of Maharashtra Dharma.
facts.quote: The Hindawi Swaraj formed by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was a State for the people, founded with the noble intention of the welfare of common people, removal of oppression and the protection of Maharashtra Dharma.

facts.text: After Shivaji Maharaj, Maratha power spread to all parts of India and lasted for about 150 years.
facts.quote: In the period after Shivaji Maharaj, Maratha power spread to all parts of India. It lasted for about 150 years.

facts.text: The Patil was responsible for the protection of the village.
facts.quote: The Patil was responsible for the protection of the village

facts.text: The Kulkarni handled the revenue of the village.
facts.quote: the Kulkarni handled the revenue.

facts.text: The Patil received land as inam for his work and also a part of the village revenue.
facts.quote: The Patil received land as inam for his work as a Patil. He also received a part of the village revenue.

facts.text: The balutedars were paid in kind (objects, foodgrains, etc.) for the work they did for the village people.
facts.quote: The balutedars were paid in kind (in the form of objects, foodgrains, etc.) for the work they did for the village people.

facts.text: There were twelve balutedars in a village, such as the blacksmith, carpenter, potter and goldsmith.
facts.quote: There were twelve balutedars such as the blacksmith, carpenter, potter, goldsmith, etc. in a village.

facts.text: Village occupations were divided into kali and pandhari: peasants worked in the kali (land, earth or soil), others in pandhari within the village precincts.
facts.quote: The village occupations were divided into kali and pandhari. Peasants worked in their fields in the kali (land, earth or soil) and others, in pandhari - within the village precincts.

facts.text: Agriculture was the major source of production in villages and the joint family system was prevalent.
facts.quote: Agriculture and occupations based on agriculture were the major sources of production at the village level. ... Joint family system was prevalent.

facts.text: Child marriages were prevalent, having many wives was acceptable and there are a few examples of widow marriages.
facts.quote: Child marriages were prevalent. It was acceptable to have many wives. There are a few examples of widow marriages in this period.

facts.text: Muhurta, or auspicious occasions, were sought for every little thing, and also to open battles.
facts.quote: Muhurta, or auspicious occasions were sought for every little thing, and also to open battles.

facts.text: Anushthans were performed to avoid the wrath of gods and planets.
facts.quote: 'Anushthans' were performed to avoid the wrath of gods and planets.

facts.text: Offerings to god (navas) were considered more important than medical treatment.
facts.quote: offerings to god (navas) were considered more important than medical treatment.

facts.text: Burning, burial and immersion methods were used to perform the last rites.
facts.quote: To perform the last rites, burning, burial and immersion methods were used as per tradition.

facts.text: Most people lived in villages, which were mostly self-sufficient; only salt had to be imported.
facts.quote: A majority of people lived in villages. The villages were mostly self-sufficient. Only salt had to be imported from other places.

facts.text: Farmers grew jowar, bajra, wheat, ragi (nachani), maize, rice and other grains.
facts.quote: They grew jowar, bajra, wheat, ragi (nachani), maize, rice and other grains in their fields.

facts.text: The daily diet was bhakari, onion, chutney and an accompaniment; rich people ate rice, dal, chapatis, vegetables, salads, milk and dahi products.
facts.quote: The daily diet consisted of bhakari, onion, chutney and an accompaniment. ... Rice, dal, chapatis, vegetables, salads, milk and dahi products were mainly included in the rich people's diet.

facts.text: Barter system was used for everyday transactions.
facts.quote: Barter system was used for everyday transactions.

facts.text: Village houses were simple mud and brick constructions; wadas with one or two storeys were seen in cities.
facts.quote: Village houses were simple mud and brick constructions. Wadas with one or two storeys were seen in cities.

facts.text: Men wore a dhoti, kurta, angarakha and mundase; women wore nine-yard sarees and blouses.
facts.quote: Men wore a dhoti, kurta, angarakha and mundase. Women wore nine-yard sarees and blouses.

facts.text: People celebrated Gudhi Padwa, Nagpanchmi, Bail-pola, Dasara, Diwali, Makarsankrant, Holi, Eid and other festivals; gudhis were raised for Gudhi Padwa.
facts.quote: People celebrated Gudhi Padwa, Nagpanchmi, Bail-pola, Dasara, Diwali, Makarsankrant, Holi, Eid and other festivals. ... Gudhis were raised to celebrate Gudhi Padwa.

facts.text: In the Peshwa period Ganeshotsava was celebrated in many homes; the Peshwa himself was a devotee of Ganesha.
facts.quote: In the Peshwa period, Ganeshotsava was celebrated in many homes. The Peshwa himself being a devotee of Ganesha, these celebrations acquired importance.

facts.text: Every year the Ganeshotsava celebrations lasted from Bhadrapad Chaturthi up to Anant Chaturdashi.
facts.quote: Every year these celebrations lasted from Bhadrapad Chaturthi up to Anant Chaturdashi.

facts.text: Dasara was considered one of the three and a half most auspicious occasions; many new things were started on this day.
facts.quote: Dasara being considered as one of the three and a half most auspicious occasions, many new things were started on this day.

facts.text: On Dasara weapons were offered puja, boundaries were crossed ceremoniously (seemollanghana) and apta leaves were distributed.
facts.quote: Weapons were offered puja, and it was customary to cross the boundaries ceremoniously (seemollanghana) and distribute 'apta' leaves on Dasara.

facts.text: The Marathas launched their campaigns after Dasara.
facts.quote: The Marathas launched their campaigns after Dasara.

facts.text: During Diwali, Balipratipada and Bhau-beej celebrations had special importance.
facts.quote: During Diwali, Balipratipada and Bhau-beej celebrations had special importance.

facts.text: Fairs (jatras) were held in most villages, with wrestling bouts; Tamasha was a popular form of entertainment.
facts.quote: In most of the villages, fairs were held. Wrestling bouts were a common feature of the fairs, (jatras). ... Tamasha was a popular form of entertainment.

facts.text: Pathshalas and madarasas imparted education; reading, writing and arithmetic were taught at home.
facts.quote: Pathshalas and madarasas were the institutes that imparted education. Reading, writing and arithmetic was taught at home.

facts.text: The modi script was used in most transactions.
facts.quote: The modi script was used in most transactions.

facts.text: Cloth, foodgrains and groceries were transported on the backs of bullocks; small boats were used in rivers; messengers and camel riders carried letters.
facts.quote: Cloth, foodgrains, groceries were transported by loading them on the backs of bullocks. Small boats were used in rivers. Messengers and camel riders carried letters to and fro.

facts.text: Wrestling and martial arts were very popular; mallakhamb, dand, lathi, dandpatta and bothati were practised.
facts.quote: Wrestling and martial arts were very popular. Mallakhamb, dand, lathi, dandpatta, bothati were practised.

facts.text: Hututu, kho-kho and atyapatya were popular outdoor games; chess, ganjifa and dice were popular indoor games.
facts.quote: Hututu, kho-kho, atyapatya were the popular outdoor games and chess, ganjifa, dice were popular indoor games.

facts.text: The two major religions were Hindu and Muslim; Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj had a liberal religious policy.
facts.quote: The two major religions seen in this period were Hindu and Muslim. Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj had a liberal religious policy.

facts.text: The government gave grants to pathshalas, temples, madarasas and mosques; followers of both religions took part in each other's festivals.
facts.quote: The government gave grants to pathshalas, temples, madarasas and mosques. Followers of both religions took part in the celebration of each other's festivals.

facts.text: Varkari, Mahanubhav, Datta, Nath and Ramdasi panths were prevalent.
facts.quote: Varkari, Mahanubhav, Datta, Nath and Ramdasi panths were prevalent.

facts.text: Women's education was neglected; exceptional women included Veermata Jijabai, Maharani Yesubai, Maharani Tarabai, Umabai Dabhade, Gopikabai and Punyashlok Ahilyabai.
facts.quote: Their education was neglected. Only a few exceptional women had achieved any progress in literacy, administration and battle skills. They include Veermata Jijabai, Maharani Yesubai, Maharani Tarabai, Umabai Dabhade, Gopikabai, Punyashlok Ahilyabai.

facts.text: Child marriage, unequal marriage, widowhood, keshwapan, sati and polygamy imposed harsh restrictions on women.
facts.quote: Customs like child marriage, unequal marriage, widowhood, keshwapan, sati, polygamy had imposed harsh restrictions on the way women lived.

facts.text: The period from 1630 CE to 1810 CE is broadly defined as Maratheshahi (it begins in 1630).
facts.quote: The period from 1630 CE to 1810 CE is broadly defined as Maratheshahi.

facts.text: Maratheshahi, broadly defined, ends in 1810 CE.
facts.quote: The period from 1630 CE to 1810 CE is broadly defined as Maratheshahi.

facts.text: Architecture of the period includes restoration of Kasba Ganapati Mandir, building of the Lal Mahal, construction on Rajgad and Raigad and building of sea forts.
facts.quote: We find references to restoration of Kasba Ganapati Mandir, building of the Lal Mahal, construction on Rajgad and Raigad, building of sea forts, etc.

facts.text: Hiroji Indulkar was a famous architect of that period.
facts.quote: Hiroji Indulkar was a famous architect of that period.

facts.text: In a new village, roads cut one another at right angles, with stone construction along the sides and extensive ghats (steps) along the river bank.
facts.quote: While setting up a village, the usual pattern was : roads cutting one another at right angles, stone construction along the sides and extensive ghats (steps) along the river bank.

facts.text: In the Peshwa period a drinking water supply system was built like the one at Ahmadnagar and Bijapur; the Peshwas built underground pipes, small dams, gardens, tanks and fountains.
facts.quote: During the Peshwa period, a drinking water supply system was built like the one at Ahmadnagar and Bijapur. The Peshwas built underground pipes, small dams, gardens and courts, tanks, fountains, etc.

facts.text: The Mastani Talav is at Diveghat, Hadapsar near Pune city.
facts.quote: The Mastani Talav at Diveghat, Hadapsar near Pune city is worth a mention in this regard.

facts.text: Shaniwarwada and Vishrambagwada in Pune, Sarkarwada in Nashik and Raghunathrao Peshwa's wada at Kopargaon are symbols of the medieval wada culture.
facts.quote: Shaniwarwada and Vishrambagwada in Pune, Sarkarwada in Nashik, Raghunathrao Peshwa's wada at Kopargaon, the wadas of the Satara Chhatrapati, as also the old wadas at Wai, Menvali, Toke, Shrigonde, Pandharpur are symbols of the medieval wada culture.

facts.text: Wadas were built with baked and unbaked bricks and decorated with sketches, paintings, wooden sculptures and mirrors.
facts.quote: Baked as well as unbaked bricks were used to build the wadas. ... The wadas were decorated with sketches, paintings, wooden sculptures and mirrors.

facts.text: The temples of this period were built in the Hemadpanti style of the Yadav period.
facts.quote: The temples of this period are build in the Hemadpanti style of the Yadav period.

facts.text: The shikhar of the Ambabai temple at Kolhapur, the temples on the Jotiba hill, the Shambhu Mahadev temple at Shikhar-Shinganapur and the Ghrishneshwar temple at Verul are excellent specimens of sculpture.
facts.quote: The shikhar of the Ambabai temple at Kolhapur, the temples on the Jotiba hill, Shambhu Mahadev temple at Shikhar-Shinganapur, Ghrishneshwar temple at Verul are excellent specimens of sculpture.

facts.text: The Bhavanidevi temple on Pratapgad and the Saptkoteshwar temple at Goa were built by Shivaji Maharaj.
facts.quote: The Bhavanidevi temple on Pratapgad and the Saptkoteshwar temple at Goa were built by Shivaji Maharaj.

facts.text: Peshwa-period temples include the Kalaram temple at Nashik, the Shiva temple at Trimbakeshwar, the Shiva temples at Kaygaon and Toke and the Mohiniraj temple at Newase.
facts.quote: Other temples of the Peshwa period are the Kalaram temple at Nashik, the Shiva temple at Trimbakeshwar, the Shiva temples at Kaygaon and Toke on the confluence of the Godavari and Pravara, and the Mohiniraj temple at Newase.

facts.text: The most remarkable ghat is at Toke, Pravara Sangam, on the confluence of the Godavari and Pravara.
facts.quote: The most remarkable specimen of a ghat is the one at Toke, Pravara Sangam on the confluence of the Godavari and Pravara.

facts.text: A ghat had one wide step at regular intervals, and strong bastions were built to prevent damage due to water currents.
facts.quote: In a flight of steps, there would be one wide step at regular intervals. ... Strong bastions were built at regular intervals so as to prevent damage due to water currents.

facts.text: The paintings on the walls of Shaniwarwada are important; Ragho, Tanaji, Anuprao, Shivram and Mankoji were important painters.
facts.quote: The paintings on the walls of Shaniwarwada are the important ones of the Peshwa period. Ragho, Tanaji, Anuprao, Shivram, Mankoji are some of the important painters of this period.

facts.text: The painter Gangaram Tambat was famous at the time of Sawai Madhavrao Peshwa; the Peshwas encouraged painting.
facts.quote: The painter Gangaram Tambat was famous at the time of Sawai Madhavrao Peshwa. The Peshwas encouraged painting.

facts.text: At Jamod in Vidarbha, Jin Charitra paintings adorned the Jain temple.
facts.quote: At Jamod in Vidarbha, Jin Charitra paintings adorned the Jain temple.

facts.text: Sculptures include the meeting between Mallamma Desai and Shivaji Maharaj at the time of his Karnataka campaign, and the memorial to Punyashlok Ahilyabai in Madhya Pradesh.
facts.quote: Important specimens include the sculpture of the meeting between Mallamma Desai and Shivaji Maharaj at the time of his Karnataka campaign, ... the memorial to Punyashlok Ahilyabai in Madhya Pradesh

facts.text: The Peshwas specially commissioned the metal idols of Parvati and Ganapati in the Parvati temple for puja.
facts.quote: The Peshwas had specially commissioned the metal idols of Parvati and Ganapati in the Parvati temple for the purpose of Puja.

facts.text: Literature forms included compositions of the Sants, teeka literature, owi, abhanga, powadas, bakhars and historical letters.
facts.quote: Important forms of literature include the compositions of the Sants, mythological narratives, 'teeka' literature, owi, abhanga, treatises, narrative poems, biographies, aaratis of deities, powadas, bakhars, historical letters, etc.

facts.text: At Tanjavur in the South, Marathi plays emerged near the end of the seventeenth century; Sarfoji Raje encouraged this art.
facts.quote: At Tanjavur in the South, Marathi plays has emerged near the end of the seventeenth century. Sarfoji Raje encouraged this art.
